summary: Phase 4 Slice D (shifts dual-write Mongo + Supabase Postgres) verified GREEN end-to-end. Backend pytest: 28/28 PASS (test_iteration13_phase4d_shifts_dualwrite.py). Direct asyncpg probes against SUPABASE_DIRECT_URL confirm: (1) POST /api/shifts (one_off) writes a row to BOTH Mongo and Postgres with caregiver_id, client_id, date (typed as date), start_time, end_time, notes, service_type, status='scheduled'; (2) PUT /api/shifts/{id} mirrors patch to PG — admin can change start_time, caregiver is restricted to notes+service_type (verified by submitting both notes and start_time as caregiver: notes was accepted, start_time was NOT modified); (3) POST /api/shifts (recurring) with weekdays MON/WED/FRI between 2026-08-03 and 2026-08-21 produces 1 parent row (kind='recurring') + exactly 9 child rows (kind='one_off', parent_shift_id=<parent>) in PG; (4) DELETE /api/shifts/<parent> for a recurring shift CASCADES — both parent and all 5 children of a TUE/THU test recurring set are removed from PG via ON DELETE CASCADE on parent_shift_id (verified count==0 after delete); (5) DELETE /api/shifts/<id> for a one_off clears PG (count==0); (6) POST /api/shifts/{id}/clock-in sets status='in_progress' in BOTH DBs, sets clocked_in_at timestamptz, and persists clock_location as JSONB in Postgres (the API takes a plain string '37.7749,-122.4194' which is wrapped via json.dumps -> stored as a JSON-encoded string in PG, verified via clock_location::text); (7) POST /api/shifts/{id}/clock-out sets status='completed' in BOTH DBs; (8) GET /api/shifts as admin returns one_off rows from Postgres with recurring parents EXCLUDED (kind='recurring' never appears in the response; the parent_id is not in the id set; the children with parent_shift_id are returned); (9) Filters caregiver_id, date range respected; (10) GET /api/shifts as caregiver returns ONLY that caregiver's shifts (Caregiver@123 token verified); (11) Supabase ES256 JWT (AdminPassword123!) also returns shifts list correctly. Phase 4 Slice A/B/C regression GREEN under BOTH legacy HS256 (Admin@123) and Supabase ES256 (AdminPassword123!) JWTs: /auth/me, /caregivers, /clients (list + detail), /stats, /documents — all 200, expected shapes (total_clients=1, total_caregivers=12, total_documents=50). Final PG parity check: api_one_off == pg_one_off (exact equality); zero orphan child shifts (no parent_shift_id points to a missing parent). After cleanup, PG shifts table back to baseline 3 rows (2 one_off + 1 recurring; 0 TEST_SliceD leftovers). Frontend regression (Expo web, mobile viewport 390x844): legacy + Admin@123 and Supabase + AdminPassword123! BOTH land on the Dashboard. Schedule tab loads with the add-shift-button visible. Verified live UI rendering of the dual-write: created a recurring shift via API (MON/WED/FRI from 2026-06-22 to 2026-07-03, 6 children); after switching to Week view in the Schedule tab, the children appear as SEPARATE individual entries on Mon Jun 22, Wed Jun 24, Fri Jun 26 (current week), and continue across the next week's dates — exactly the expected one_off expansion. The recurring parent row does NOT leak into the UI list (verified by checking the on-screen testIDs against the parent's UUID). Team and Documents tabs still render (Test Client Jones row visible on Team; Document Vault still loads). No new expo/react-native deprecation issues introduced by Slice D.
critical_code_review_comments: routers/shifts.py:84 — db.shifts.insert_many(children) followed by supa_data.upsert_shifts_bulk(children) iterates one-at-a-time in PG (one round-trip per child via upsert_shift). For a year-long recurring schedule that's up to 366 sequential round-trips. Consider using executemany() or a single VALUES clause for the bulk path.

routers/shifts.py:212 — clock_in stores req.location as-is. supa_data._shift_clock_location wraps non-dict/list values into json.dumps(str(v)), so '37.7749,-122.4194' is stored in PG as the JSON string "37.7749,-122.4194" (with quotes). If the long-term plan is structured geo data (lat/lng object), the Mongo schema should be tightened now — Pydantic accepts arbitrary strings today, which makes downstream parsing brittle.

routers/shifts.py:179 — Mongo cascade for recurring children is db.shifts.delete_many({'parent_shift_id': d['id']}), but PG relies on ON DELETE CASCADE. Two write paths means if Mongo ever drifts (manual fix-up, schema change) the cascades could diverge. Once Slice J flips reads to PG, consider dropping the explicit Mongo cascade and letting PG be authoritative.

routers/shifts.py:117-123 — list_shifts always sets one_off_only=True, which is correct, but the supa_data helper signature still exposes it. Once the API is the only caller, hard-code the filter in the SQL helper to prevent accidental misuse.

core/supa_data.py:507 — upsert_shifts_bulk runs N separate connection acquisitions inside a loop (each upsert_shift acquires a pool connection). Better: pass a single conn through, or batch via copy_records_to_table. Same hotspot as routers/shifts.py:84.

core/supa_data.py:566 (list_shifts_filtered) — query rebuilds string via list-join every call; not a perf issue at current scale but harder to test. Consider parameterised builder (e.g., a small SQL fragment helper).

context_for_next_testing_agent: Phase 4 Slice D is GREEN. ALL mutating shift routes (POST /shifts, PUT /shifts/{id}, DELETE /shifts/{id}, POST /shifts/{id}/clock-in, POST /shifts/{id}/clock-out) now dual-write Mongo + Postgres. GET /api/shifts READS from Postgres (one_off_only=True) — Mongo is no longer consulted for the schedule list. Recurring parents (kind='recurring') are excluded from the response; children (kind='one_off' with parent_shift_id) are returned individually. clock_location is jsonb in PG; the helper supa_data._shift_clock_location wraps plain strings via json.dumps. ON DELETE CASCADE on parent_shift_id handles recurring children cleanup in PG. Reusable test fixtures in test_iteration13_phase4d_shifts_dualwrite.py: legacy_token, supabase_token, caregiver_legacy_token, H/Hsupa/Hcg header fixtures, the_client_id session fixture (sole client UUID), pg_fetchrow/pg_fetchval/pg_fetch with new event-loop-safe runner. Frontend tab navigation works by clicking the text label (page.get_by_text('Schedule', exact=True).first); Schedule view uses testIDs view-day, view-week, nav-prev, nav-today, nav-next, add-shift-button, shift-<uuid>, clock-in-<uuid>, clock-out-<uuid>. Next slice is presumably Phase 4 Slice E (onboarding or training dual-write), or Slice J cutover (drop Mongo writes).
